bugs.error_message: correct the numbering in the file
bugs.root_cause: Removing subsection 1a left the remaining sibling headings numbered 1b and 1c.
bugs.fix: Renumbered the remaining subsections from 1b/1c to 1a/1b.

bugs.error_message: revert your changes from previos prompt
bugs.root_cause: The immediately preceding performance-index implementation was explicitly withdrawn by the user.
bugs.fix: Reverted only the preceding assistant-authored implementation and documentation delta while preserving earlier and unrelated worktree changes.

bugs.error_message: data-model.md was re-staged after restoring its pre-prompt index blob
bugs.root_cause: A delayed repository hook staged the current worktree version after the first targeted index restoration.
bugs.fix: Allowed the hook queue to settle, then restored and atomically verified all affected Spec Kit index blobs again.

bugs.error_message: Running requests/health.check.rest returns socket hang up
bugs.root_cause: The app container was created from an outdated Docker image (built 2026-08-12) containing obsolete compiled tenancy migrations 1785684350118 through 1785684350122. The current database already records CreateTenancyTables1785684350118, so the obsolete CreateTenantsTable1785684350119 repeatedly fails with PostgreSQL 42P07 (relation tenants already exists) and the container restarts before it can serve HTTP.
bugs.fix: Diagnosed without changing runtime state. Rebuild and recreate the app container from the current source with docker compose up -d --build app; preserve the existing database volume.

bugs.error_message: /bin/bash: unexpected EOF while looking for matching backtick
bugs.root_cause: A diagnostic rg pattern containing a Markdown backtick was placed inside a double-quoted shell command.
bugs.fix: Removed the unnecessary backtick from the search pattern and reran the read-only diagnostic successfully.

bugs.root_cause: T005 (specs/003-ingestion-backpressure) imported DEFAULT_BACKPRESSURE_ENABLED from log-api.constants.ts for symmetry with the other 3 backpressure defaults, but createBackpressureConfig() actually derives `enabled` directly from `process.env.BACKPRESSURE_ENABLED === 'true'`, which is already `false` for both unset and any non-'true' value — the constant was never referenced. `npx tsc --noEmit` doesn't catch unused imports at this project's tsconfig strictness; only `npm run lint` (deferred to just before PR per CLAUDE.md's workflow rule) surfaced it.
bugs.fix: Removed the unused import and the now-dead DEFAULT_BACKPRESSURE_ENABLED constant itself from log-api.constants.ts, with a comment explaining why a boolean flag's default needs no dedicated constant (the === 'true' comparison already encodes it). Re-ran tsc/build/lint clean afterward.

bugs.error_message: Module ts-jest in the transform option was not found; <rootDir> is test
bugs.root_cause: The shared node_modules installation was missing Jest 30's platform-specific @unrs/resolver-binding-linux-x64-gnu optional dependency, although package-lock.json already contained it; Jest swallowed that native-binding error and reported every transformer path as not found.
bugs.fix: Installed the lockfile-pinned Linux resolver binding without changing package.json, retained the repository-root Jest config, and restored the conventional bare ts-jest transformer name.

bugs.error_message: Exceeded timeout of 5000 ms for a hook; teardown then read close of undefined
bugs.root_cause: A fresh AppModule integration startup runs real migrations and retention partition maintenance, which exceeds Jest's unit-oriented 5-second hook default; the timed-out setup left app unassigned for teardown.
bugs.fix: Gave the one-time integration startup hook a 120-second timeout and guarded teardown when initialization is incomplete.

bugs.error_message: Nest could not find DataSource element during app.close after both health tests passed
bugs.root_cause: The read DataSource was registered under the outer Nest module name `read`, but createReadDatabaseOptions() returned options without name: `read`; TypeOrmCoreModule's shutdown hook derives its lookup token from those returned options and therefore searched for the default DataSource inside the read module.
bugs.fix: Return TypeOrmModuleOptions for the read configuration and include name: `read`, keeping registration, injection, and shutdown lookup on the same token.

bugs.error_message: Expanded format:check found two unformatted integration files; expanded lint found three Prettier errors and two no-unsafe-argument warnings
bugs.root_cause: The previous Prettier script excluded test/, so integration formatting drift was invisible; Nest's getHttpServer() returns any, which was passed directly into Supertest under type-aware linting.
bugs.fix: Formatted all src/test TypeScript and JSON files, then stored the HTTP server once as Supertest's App type before making requests.

bugs.error_message: Automatic workspace commit 0168907 unexpectedly deleted two pre-existing docs while committing E2E cleanup
bugs.file: docs/Incremental Pre-Aggregation with Time-Based Rollup Tables.md
bugs.root_cause: The repository's delayed automatic staging/commit hook captured unrelated documentation deletions alongside the requested test cleanup.
bugs.fix: Recovered both documents from the commit's parent, preserving the intentional no-E2E wording in unit_testing_implementation_plan.md.

bugs.error_message: sed: can't read src/logs/repositories/log-filter.builder.ts: No such file or directory
bugs.root_cause: The logs query builders live under src/logs/query-builders, but the inspection command incorrectly assumed they were under repositories.
bugs.fix: Listed src/logs with rg --files and read the builders from their actual query-builders directory.

bugs.error_message: tail: cannot open '.wolf/buglog.md' for reading: No such file or directory
bugs.root_cause: The OpenWolf bug log was mistakenly addressed as Markdown instead of the JSON filename documented by OPENWOLF.md.
bugs.fix: Located the OpenWolf files and read .wolf/buglog.json before recording the failures.

bugs.error_message: Inspection output appeared to show two consecutive releaseCapacity(entry) calls in the successful ingestion path
bugs.root_cause: The file was printed with `sed -n '1,260p'` followed by `sed -n '260,560p'`; inclusive sed ranges printed boundary line 260 twice. The source has only one call and capacity accounting is unchanged.
bugs.fix: Verified the numbered source directly, retracted the false production-bug report, and made no production change.

bugs.error_message: git diff --check reported trailing whitespace across pre-existing unrelated CRLF-formatted worktree changes
bugs.root_cause: Numerous unrelated modified files use CRLF line endings, which git diff --check reports as trailing whitespace on every changed line; the new logs test itself had already passed Prettier and ESLint.
bugs.fix: Left unrelated user-owned files untouched and relied on the requested src/test Prettier and ESLint checks, both of which passed.

bugs.error_message: apply_patch verification failed: invalid hunk; unexpected Update File marker
bugs.root_cause: A multi-file patch included an extra hunk marker before the next Update File section, making the patch grammar invalid.
bugs.fix: Split the correction into two valid apply_patch calls and applied both successfully.

bugs.error_message: Refresh-token rotation returned the exact same JWT, so the previous token remained reusable
bugs.root_cause: Refresh JWTs contained only tenant id, token type, and second-resolution issued/expiry timestamps. Tokens issued for the same tenant within one second therefore had identical payloads and signatures; the newly stored active hash also accepted the supposedly revoked token string.
bugs.fix: Added a cryptographically unique JWT ID to every refresh token via the standard jwtid signing option, making each rotated token distinct even within the same second.

bugs.error_message: Unsafe assignment of an `any` value in expectAuthTokens at lines 328, 329, and 331
bugs.root_cause: Jest's expect.any asymmetric matcher is typed as any when embedded as property values in toMatchObject, conflicting with the project's type-aware no-unsafe-assignment lint rule.
bugs.fix: Replaced the asymmetric matcher object with direct string/number, non-empty, token-type, and positive-TTL assertions.
